site.title: Travis Minor — Roboticist
site.tagline: I build autonomy and control software for real robots.

about.heading: About
about.summary: I'm a Computer Science student at the University at Buffalo, minoring in Robotics and Math. I work on field robotics at DRONESLab and lead autonomy work on student rover teams. I care most about robot software that holds up outside the lab: navigation, SLAM, teleoperation and safety-critical control.
highlights: B.S. Computer Science, Minor in Robotics and Math — University at Buffalo, expected Dec. 2026
Undergraduate researcher at DRONESLab, building open-source control software for Boston Dynamics Spot
Led autonomy for NASA LunaBotics and 15 engineers across 4 subteams at UB SpaceBulls

projects.name: VISION-Inspect
projects.description: VISION-Inspect sends Spot out to inspect infrastructure like culverts and look for damage. Instead of stopping to take pictures on a fixed schedule, the robot uses its sensors and an AI vision model to decide what's worth a closer look. I'm also testing whether the model can find defects in kinds of structures it has never seen before.

projects.name: Open-Spot: Spot Operator
projects.description: Spot Operator lets a person drive and control Boston Dynamics' Spot robot dog from a handheld Steam Deck. It's part of open-spot, DRONESLab's open-source toolkit for Spot, and it's the base the lab builds its research on. It's designed to be safe first: if the connection drops or something crashes, the robot stops, and the emergency stop always works.

projects.name: NASA LunaBotics Rover
projects.description: UB's rover for NASA's LunaBotics competition, where university teams build robots that work on their own in simulated lunar terrain. I built its autonomy system, which lets the rover figure out where it is using its cameras, plan a path, and recover when it gets stuck, all without a driver. I led the autonomy subteam that took it from not working at all to ready for competition.

projects.name: UB SpaceBulls Rover
projects.description: The rover built by UB SpaceBulls, the university's student robotics club. I worked on the software on its onboard hardware and built a simulated version of the rover in Gazebo, so the team could test changes on a computer before running them on the real robot. Along the way I went from leading one subteam to leading the whole project.

projects.name: Catan Agent
projects.description: Catan Agent is an AI that taught itself to play Settlers of Catan through trial and error. It reads the board as a graph of connected tiles and settlements, so it can play on any board layout, not just the one it trained on. During training its opponents got tougher as it started winning more, which helped it improve faster.
